The main takeaway from our work is that

, in realistic scenarios, a Network-MIMO architecture based on small clusters of cooperating cells and a suitable inter-cluster interference management can achieve spectral efficiencies close to "Massive MISO" with one order of smaller number of antennas per active user, and thus can be implemented in practice with significantly lower hardware complexity.

, by exploiting channel correlation across users and across cells, the proposed architecture achieves the same spectral efficiencies of the "Massive Mimo" architecture with one order of magnitudes fewer antennas.

, in the large-system regime, the proposed Network-MIMO scheme achieves the same order of magnitude of spectral efficiency as Massive MIMO, with a number of antennas per active user roughly one order of magnitude smaller.
